correctness.rationale: The two reset-free Gaussian pairs are derived from stochastic integrals and conditional Gaussian velocity. Exact differentiation gives two functions G with one sign change each: both use positive error-function integral representations E(z) and E'(z)/E(z)<=1/z, so their root-ratio log derivatives are strictly negative. The positive and negative pieces of t h'(t) live on separated time supports, giving a strictly increasing ratio of exponentially tilted Laplace contributions and therefore exactly one reset-rate critical point. Both endpoints of the intensity vanish. Explicit reproducibility calculations verify covariance normalizations, derivatives, and integral roots; numerical tests are not mistaken for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact Poisson-renewal formula, reset-free Gaussian Kac–Rice kernels, and existence/plots of an optimal rate are acknowledged as prior work; the assessed advance is a proof that both explicitly studied canonical scaling functions have exactly one critical rate, a strict global maximum, with computable dimensionless constants. The main full text explains it did not solve the first maximizer integral equation, and neither canonical case is proved unique there. External searches and accessible related records provided no implication establishing the two sign inequalities. Residual broader-theorem coverage is possible; publication priority is not certified.
residual_risks: No external independent mathematical review; full publication priority is not guaranteed by negative searches.
A broader theorem on total-positivity or Rice kernels might imply the one-peak special-function inequalities.
The dimensional optimal rates and peak intensities are model-specific; they do not extend to damped, partial, or non-Poisson resetting without new arguments.

value.rationale: The underlying paper motivates optimizing crossing counts but leaves both global optimizer structures analytically unresolved. The theorem excludes secondary local maxima for two physically distinct complete-reset protocols, proves exact one-crossing special-function inequalities, and supplies universal calibrations for the optimal Poisson clocks. This resolves a natural whole-parameter optimization problem, not a small arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recalculation.
